title: Ghost in the Machine v7 — preregistration: which part of the prediction error must be in step, a powered test of Psi, and a robust gain test
author: Kai Piper
scientific_status: Synthetic computational experiment. No hypothesis below concerns, measures or can establish phenomenal consciousness.
background: v6 (lock 88b10c2, results 0d4a521) showed that the authorship effect on self persistence is carried by the comparator's prediction-error stream (transplants: 0.08 and 0.85 of the effect) and, by its preregistered decision rule, depends on that stream being in step with the network's own state: desynchronizing the author's own stream, which keeps every value and the spectrum, keeps only 0.60 of the effect.

Open question 1: the live error m_t = obs_t - forward_model(x_t, intention_t) depends on the network's current state, so the comparator is also a feedback loop. Is the in-step benefit the loop (the part of the error the state predicts) or the alignment of the rest?

Open question 2 (v6, unexplained): a twin given the author's stream reached 0.85 of the effect while the author given its own desynchronized stream reached 0.60, as if synchrony mattered for the author but not for the twin.

Open question 3: Psi. The preregistered v5 replication missed (d_z 0.20); v6 Study G found d_z 0.55 (secondary); a post-hoc random-effects meta-analysis over five samples gave +0.129 [0.077, 0.181], pooled d_z 0.36, I^2 0.20. No single preregistered sample so far was sized for an effect of that size.

Open question 4: v6 Study J (comparator gain) was inconclusive because two of 24 networks had near-frozen twins (persistence 2.0-2.6 nats), which dominate a mean test on the unbounded Gaussian persistence.
code: ghost_v4, ghost_v5 and ghost_v6 frozen (their locks keep verifying); ghost_v7.engine mirrors ghost_v6.engine and reproduces it bit for bit at default settings; with both parts of the split live it reproduces the live run (tests/test_v7.py). Unit tests ran on tiny development runs (400 cycles, seeds 100-102) to check the code; their numbers were not inspected.
decomposition: For each master, the mismatch at cycle t is regressed (ridge, penalty 1e-3 times the mean eigenvalue of the state covariance) on the network state entering cycle t, over the analysis window of its live run: f_t = c + B x_t is the state-predicted ('feedback') part and i_t = m_t - f_t the rest ('innovation'). In a run, from cycle burn on, either part can be replaced by its own recorded stream circularly shifted by half the window (as in v6 Study G) while the other part is computed live from the current state and the current mismatch. pe_state_r2 (the share of mismatch variance the state predicts) is reported for every run.

robust_methods.self_rho: Bounded persistence: the lag-1 autocorrelation of the self population's maximum-autocorrelation feature V over the analysis window. It is the exact bounded form of the Gaussian persistence (I = -0.5 log(1 - rho^2)).
robust_methods.signed_rank: Wilcoxon signed-rank test computed by sign-flipping the ranks of |d| (exact for n <= 16, else 20000 flips), one-sided in the stated direction; the effect is reported as the Hodges-Lehmann estimate with a 95% bootstrap CI, the median and the count of positive networks.

test: Unless a hypothesis names the robust test, the paired sign-flip test on the mean as in v4-v6 (exact for n <= 16, else 20000 flips), one-sided in the stated direction, with mean difference, 95% bootstrap CI and d_z.

equivalence.rationale: Persistence: about a third of the v4 / replication authorship effect (as in v6). Psi: a third of the v4 confirmatory H4 mean difference.

multiplicity: Holm within each study's primary family (the confirmatory decision). Holm across all v7 primary tests is also reported.

K.name: feedback vs innovation
K.design: Conditions in the analysis window. Master (network s in its own live world): live; shift (its own live mismatch desynchronized, exactly as v6 G 'shift'); fbLive_innShift (feedback part live from the current state, innovation part = its own recorded innovation desynchronized); fbShift_innLive (feedback part = its own recorded feedback desynchronized, innovation part live). Twin (network s cross-yoked to the next network's master stream): live; shift (its own live mismatch desynchronized).

hypotheses.statement: desynchronization costs the author (replicates v6 G3)
a live state-feedback part restores persistence
a live innovation part restores persistence
synchrony matters more for the author than for the twin
hypotheses.statistic: [master live - master shift] - [twin live - twin shift] (self_persistence)

K.decision_rule: account = 'both' if K2 and K3 are significant (Holm); 'feedback' if K2 is significant and K3 is equivalent to zero (TOST, 0.04 nats); 'innovation' if K3 is significant and K2 is equivalent to zero; otherwise 'undetermined'.
K.secondary: Fraction of the desynchronization loss each part recovers (bootstrap CI); robust (self_rho, signed-rank) versions of K1-K4; pe_state_r2 in master vs twin live runs (does the state predict more of an author's error?); injected RMS per condition (manipulation check); authorship effect (master live - twin live).

L.name: powered test of authorship-dependent causal emergence
L.design: Master and cross-yoked twin, default architecture and comparator, as in v4. 72 networks give about 92% power for a one-sided test at d_z = 0.36 (the pooled estimate), ignoring between-sample heterogeneity.

hypotheses.statement: authorship raises Psi of the self population's slow mode

L.secondary: Psi equivalence test (bound 0.0561); Psi signed-rank; Gaussian persistence mean test; Psi macro and parts terms; pe_state_r2 master minus twin.

M.name: comparator gain with a robust measure
M.design: As v6 Study J with twice the networks: master and cross-yoked twin with the injected comparator term multiplied by k in {0.5, 1, 2} (the twin at gain k is yoked to the donor's master at the same gain).

hypotheses.statement: the authorship effect is present at half gain
hypotheses.statistic: self_rho(master) - self_rho(twin) at k = 0.5, signed-rank test

hypotheses.statement: the authorship effect grows with the gain
hypotheses.statistic: [self_rho(master) - self_rho(twin)] at k = 2 minus the same at k = 0.5, signed-rank test

M.secondary: Robust effect at each gain; Gaussian mean-test versions (as v6 J); master and twin bounded persistence from k = 0.5 to 2.

prespecified_exploratory.cumulative_meta_analysis: Random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird) pooling of master - twin differences, with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman CI, leave-one-out estimates and a 95% prediction interval, for self persistence (nats), self_rho and Psi, over exactly these samples: v4 confirmatory (48), v5 A replication (48), v5 F standard wiring (24), v6 G live (48), v6 J gain 1 (24), v7 K live (48), v7 L (72), v7 M gain 1 (48). For samples before v7, self_rho is computed from the stored Gaussian persistence by the exact identity rho = sqrt(1 - exp(-2 I)), which is checked on v7 L data. Also a signed-rank test over all networks pooled.
prespecified_exploratory.status: Exploratory: the earlier samples have been seen. Fixed here, before any v7 data, so that the new samples cannot select the analysis.

pilot_policy: A technical pilot of K, L and M on six development networks (seeds 100-105, world 1, already examined in v4 development) is run after this document is committed and pushed, and before locking. Its purpose is to catch software faults. Its results are recorded here; hypotheses, directions, bounds and the decision rule may not be changed because of them.
deviations_policy: Any deviation from this document is reported as such in the results and the paper.
